How to Write Better Alt Text for Service Websites

2026-04-15 4 min read

Alt text should support the purpose of the page. It does not need to describe everything, but it should never leave meaningful images unexplained.

Alt text works best when it reflects why the image is there. A team photo on an about page may need short identification, while a process graphic may need a more functional description that explains the information being communicated.

One common mistake is writing very generic alt text like image, banner, or team photo. Another is stuffing too many keywords into the description. Both approaches make the experience worse for screen reader users.

Service businesses should review homepage visuals, trust badges, before-and-after images, and process diagrams to make sure the text alternative matches what a user needs to understand.
